---
title: "Gene-set enrichment"
description: >
  Plot over-representation and GSEA results from clusterProfiler, fgsea or the
  GSEA application: standardize_enrichment(), plot_enrichment_dots(),
  plot_enrichment_bars(), plot_enrichment_grid(), plot_gsea_rank() and
  format_gene_sets().
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_common.R")
```

**Question:** which pathways or gene programs are enriched among the genes
that change, in one comparison or across many?

| Function | Shows | Input |
|---|---|---|
| `standardize_enrichment()` | one table from any tool (used by every plot below) | fgsea, clusterProfiler, GSEA desktop |
| `plot_enrichment_dots()` | the top gene sets of one or a few results | ORA or GSEA |
| `plot_enrichment_bars()` | NES of the top up and down gene sets of one comparison | GSEA |
| `plot_enrichment_grid()` | gene sets × comparisons | ORA or GSEA |
| `plot_gsea_rank()` | the running enrichment score of one gene set | GSEA with the ranked list |
| `format_gene_sets()` | gene sets as a list, GMT or GeneSetCollection | |

The two kinds of analysis answer different questions.
**Over-representation (ORA)** tests whether a gene list (e.g. up-regulated
genes) contains more genes of a set than expected; the result depends on the
cutoffs that made the list. **GSEA** ranks all genes (e.g. by signed
significance) and tests whether a set's genes gather at the top or bottom of
the ranking; its normalized enrichment score (NES) is signed.

**Data:** MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (msigdbr, human). GSEA: interferon-β (IFN-β)
vs control per cell type in the PBMCs of
[Kang et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042) (pseudobulk edgeR, see
[DE: many comparisons](de-multi.html)). ORA: genes up- and down-regulated by
IFN-γ in the macrophages of
[Alasoo et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-018-0046-7).

## Gene sets

```{r gene-sets}
# msigdbr::msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "H"), cached
hallmark <- docs_hallmark()
hallmark_list <- split(hallmark$gene_symbol, hallmark$gs_name)
length(hallmark_list)
```

`format_gene_sets()` converts between a named list (the input of fgsea and
`Seurat::AddModuleScore()`), a GMT file and a GSEABase `GeneSetCollection`:

```{r format-gene-sets}
gmt_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".gmt")
# Write a GMT file, then read it back as a list
format_gene_sets(hallmark_list, to = "gmt", file = gmt_file)
substr(readLines(gmt_file, n = 2), 1, 70)
sets <- format_gene_sets(gmt_file, to = "list")
identical(sets, lapply(hallmark_list, unique))
```

## Running the analyses

GSEA with fgsea, per cell type. The ranking metric is the signed
−log10 p-value of each gene (adjusted p-values have many ties):

```{r gsea}
de <- docs_kang_de()
signed_p <- function(t) {
    stats <- -log10(t$PValue) * sign(t$logFC)
    sort(setNames(stats, rownames(t)), decreasing = TRUE)
}
ranks <- lapply(de, signed_p)
set.seed(1)
# eps = 0: estimate very small p-values exactly (fgsea's recommendation)
gsea <- lapply(ranks, function(r) {
    fgsea::fgsea(hallmark_list, r, minSize = 15, maxSize = 500, eps = 0)
})
```

ORA with clusterProfiler, for the genes up- and down-regulated by IFN-γ in
macrophages (edgeR, paired by donor), against all tested genes as the
universe:

```{r ora}
mac <- docs_macrophage()
keep <- mac$samples$condition %in% c("naive", "IFNg")
samples <- droplevels(mac$samples[keep, ])
counts <- filter_low_expression_genes(mac$counts[, keep], 6)
y <- edgeR::normLibSizes(edgeR::DGEList(counts))
design <- model.matrix(~ donor + condition, data = samples)
fit <- edgeR::glmQLFit(y, design)
test <- edgeR::glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "conditionIFNg")
de_ifng <- as.data.frame(edgeR::topTags(test, n = Inf))
lists <- filter_de_genes(de_ifng, logfc.cutoff = 1)

term2gene <- hallmark[c("gs_name", "gene_symbol")]
ora <- lapply(lists, function(d) {
    clusterProfiler::enricher(
        rownames(d),
        TERM2GENE = term2gene,
        universe = rownames(de_ifng)
    )
})
names(ora) <- c("Up in IFN-γ", "Down in IFN-γ")
```

## Reading results

Every plot reads its input with `standardize_enrichment()`, which recognises
fgsea, clusterProfiler (GSEA and ORA) and GSEA desktop tables, and makes
MSigDB names readable (`clean.terms`: "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE"
becomes "Interferon alpha response"; the original is kept in `term_id`):

```{r standardize, message = TRUE}
std <- standardize_enrichment(gsea)
top_rows <- std[order(std$padj), c("term", "comparison", "nes", "padj", "size")]
head(top_rows, 4)
```

A named list gives one comparison per element; a clusterProfiler result
object can be passed as it is.

## Top gene sets: dot plot

The most significant gene sets of a result. For ORA, the x-axis is the gene
ratio (genes of the set in the list / genes in the list), the size the number
of genes and the colour the −log10 adjusted p-value. One result is one panel,
with its colour bar and size legend side by side:

```{r dots-one}
plot_enrichment_dots(ora[["Up in IFN-γ"]], n = 8)
```

A GSEA result alone, on the NES (sizes: leading-edge genes):

```{r dots-one-gsea}
plot_enrichment_dots(gsea[["CD14 Mono"]], x = "nes", n = 8)
```

A named list gives one panel per result, each in its own palette. All strips
have the same thickness, their names centred, and the legends sit in two
columns: the colour bars of the panels (top panel first), then the size
legend (one, since the panels share their limits):

```{r dots}
plot_enrichment_dots(ora, n = 8)
```

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `x = "nes"`

GSEA results on the NES; several cell types side by side (`nrow = 1`):

```{r dots-nes}
plot_enrichment_dots(
    gsea[c("CD14 Mono", "B")],
    x = "nes",
    n = 6,
    nrow = 1
)
```

#### `order.by` and `term.replace`

Ordered by significance, with shortened names:

```{r dots-replace}
plot_enrichment_dots(
    ora,
    n = 6,
    order.by = "padj",
    term.replace = c("Interferon" = "IFN", " response" = "")
)
```

#### `shared.scale`

`shared.scale = FALSE` gives each panel its own colour and size range, when
the results differ in strength; each panel then has its own size legend:

```{r dots-scale}
plot_enrichment_dots(ora, n = 6, shared.scale = FALSE, cols = "seq-blue")
```

#### `legend.layout = "stacked"`

All legends in one column, each panel's colour bar and size legend in turn:

```{r dots-stacked}
plot_enrichment_dots(ora, n = 6, legend.layout = "stacked")
```

## One comparison: NES bars

The top gene sets with positive and negative NES of one comparison; names
sit on the opposite side of 0 from their bars:

```{r bars}
plot_enrichment_bars(gsea, comparison = "CD14 Mono", n.up = 6, n.down = 6)
```

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `fill = "padj"`

```{r bars-padj}
plot_enrichment_bars(
    gsea,
    comparison = "CD14 Mono",
    n.up = 6,
    n.down = 6,
    fill = "padj"
)
```

#### `show.ns`

Non-significant gene sets fill the bars when there are fewer significant ones,
faded:

```{r bars-ns}
plot_enrichment_bars(
    gsea,
    comparison = "B",
    n.up = 5,
    n.down = 5,
    show.ns = TRUE
)
```

## Many comparisons: grid

Gene sets × comparisons: colour is the NES (centred on 0, each side to its
own extreme), size the −log10 adjusted p-value, non-significant results
faded; by default the top `n` sets of each comparison, clustered:

```{r grid}
plot_enrichment_grid(gsea, n = 4)
```

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `terms`

Chosen gene sets, in groups of rows marked by bars:

```{r grid-terms}
chosen <- list(
    Interferon = c("Interferon alpha response", "Interferon gamma response"),
    Inflammation = c("Inflammatory response", "TNFA signaling via NFKB", "IL6 JAK STAT3 signaling"),
    Proliferation = c("E2F targets", "G2M checkpoint", "MYC targets v1")
)
plot_enrichment_grid(gsea, terms = chosen)
```

#### ORA

Over-representation results are coloured by significance and sized by the
number of genes:

```{r grid-ora}
plot_enrichment_grid(ora, n = 6)
```

#### `significance` and `flip`

```{r grid-flip}
plot_enrichment_grid(gsea, n = 3, significance = "hide", flip = TRUE)
```

## One gene set: running score

`plot_gsea_rank()` draws the running enrichment score of a gene set along the
ranked list, the positions of its genes, and the ranking metric. From fgsea
results, give the ranked list (`stats`) and the gene sets. The first five
genes of the leading edge (the set's genes before the peak of the score) are
named, with an arrow to their ticks:

```{r rank}
plot_gsea_rank(
    gsea,
    "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE",
    comparison = "CD14 Mono",
    stats = ranks[["CD14 Mono"]],
    gene.sets = hallmark_list,
    metric.title = "Signed\n-log10 p"
)
```

The band under the gene positions is the ranking metric along the list, as
in the GSEA desktop plot: magenta where genes rank up (metric above 0), white
around 0, blue where they rank down. It is the same for every gene set of a
comparison and shows where the list turns from up- to down-ranked genes
(the dashed line in the metric panel). It is not the band of
`enrichplot::gseaplot2()`, which colours eight stretches of the list holding
equal shares of the set's genes and encodes no value at the rank where it is
drawn.

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### Negative score

The gene set with the most significant negative NES in CD14 monocytes; its
leading edge is at the end of the list, named from the most down-ranked gene:

```{r rank-negative}
mono <- gsea[["CD14 Mono"]]
negative_set <- mono$pathway[which.min(ifelse(mono$NES < 0, mono$padj, Inf))]
plot_gsea_rank(
    gsea,
    negative_set,
    comparison = "CD14 Mono",
    stats = ranks[["CD14 Mono"]],
    gene.sets = hallmark_list,
    metric.title = "Signed\n-log10 p"
)
```

#### Chosen genes

`label = "selected"` names the genes given (`label.features`); `"none"`
names none. `band = "none"` leaves the band out:

```{r rank-selected}
plot_gsea_rank(
    gsea,
    "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE",
    comparison = "CD14 Mono",
    stats = ranks[["CD14 Mono"]],
    gene.sets = hallmark_list,
    label = "selected",
    label.features = c("ISG15", "IFIT1", "MX1"),
    band = "none"
)
```

#### clusterProfiler

A clusterProfiler `GSEA()` result holds the ranked list and the gene sets,
so it is plotted directly; a gene set can also be named by its cleaned name:

```{r rank-cp}
cp <- clusterProfiler::GSEA(
    ranks[["B"]],
    TERM2GENE = term2gene,
    pvalueCutoff = 1,
    eps = 0,
    seed = TRUE,
    verbose = FALSE
)
plot_gsea_rank(
    cp,
    "Interferon gamma response",
    comparison = "B",
    metric.title = "Signed\n-log10 p"
)
```
